description_short.value: Ghanaian oil marketing group supplying fuel and lubricants mainly to mines, with a retail station network, a Takoradi gasoil terminal and its own tanker fleet; listed in April 2026 and 80% owned by its founder.
description_short.source: Written by us from the ZEN Petroleum Holdings PLC IPO Prospectus dated 17 March 2026 (sections 3.1-3.3) and the unaudited statements for the six months to 30 September 2026

description_full.value: ZEN Petroleum Holdings PLC is the holding company of the ZEN group, which imports, stores, transports and sells petroleum products in Ghana. William Tewiah founded the business in 2010; its main operating company, ZEN Petroleum Ltd, was incorporated in 2012 and licensed as an oil marketing company in 2013. ZEN's core market is the mining sector: the prospectus estimates it supplies about 49% of the fuel used by Ghana's major mines, from depots at sites including Tarkwa, Ayanfuri, Manso Nkran, Bolgatanga and Kenyasi, and it also sells lubricants and marine gasoil and runs more than 60 retail service stations. Its other subsidiaries are Astra Oil Services, a bulk importer and distributor; ZEN Terminals, which owns a 30,000-tonne gasoil depot at New Takoradi; and two haulage companies, ZEN Transport and Ladybird Logistics, the latter run with an all-female driver team. National Petroleum Authority figures for January to August 2026 placed it fourth among Ghana's oil marketing companies. The holding company was incorporated on 9 December 2025 to take over these subsidiaries and listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange on 22 April 2026, after an initial public offer of 128 million new shares at GHS 5.00 that raised GHS 640 million. Mr Tewiah keeps 512 million of the 640 million shares (80%). The group's year ends on 31 March. On the combined basis in its prospectus, revenue grew from GHS 5.1 billion in the year to March 2023 to GHS 6.3 billion in the year to March 2025, and profit after tax from GHS 212 million to GHS 388 million.
